comments.text:
WHAT
Separate the EXPECTATION from the RECEIPT in docs/demos/STATUS.tsv so a row's number cannot be
validated against a file the row's own author wrote. Today scripts/lane-status.sh verifies that a
cited receipt EXISTS on disk (fail-closed, exit 3, RED arm proven with a planted bogus row). It does
not verify that the receipt's VALUE agrees with a separately-recorded expectation. Existence is not
agreement.

WHY
This is the lane's most-measured defect class, not a speculative one.
  * Three candidates were scored both ways and all three fell the same direction — authored
    success, real-data miss: a gate at 0/20 FP authored vs 3/20 held-out; foreman supervision
    AUC 1.000 on vignettes vs 0.750 on 186,449 real windows; jev-review 12/12 authored pairs vs
    AUC 0.625 on 22 real diffs (RULING-authored-vs-real-20260919.md).
  * R70: "our kills are auditable, our ships are not" — FP samples were never persisted, so a
    number existed that nobody but its author could check.
  * 2026-09-21: a 219-row corpus was reported with aggregates only and no pair identities. Caught
    by a peer, not by a gate. A validator that checks existence would have passed it.
  * Same day, dumpTools was cited as an L2 oracle by two panes; it is blind to extension tools. A
    value check against an independent expectation would have caught the false ZERO; an existence
    check would not.

ACCEPTANCE
  Command: ./scripts/lane-status.sh   (plus its selftest)
  POSITIVE: every STATUS.tsv row carries an expectation field recorded independently of the
    receipt, and lane-status.sh exits 0 only when receipt value == expectation for every row.
  PLANTED NEGATIVE (required, must be shown failing): a row whose receipt EXISTS but whose value
    DISAGREES with its expectation must exit non-zero. The current validator passes that case —
    demonstrate the current pass, then the new fail. Without both halves this is unproven.
  NO-CLAIM: this gates arithmetic agreement only. It does not detect a wrong expectation, a
    corpus the author also chose, or a metric that is the wrong metric.

CREATION GATE (tick.md section 1 — all four named)
  1. CONSUMER: scripts/lane-status.sh, and every pane that cites a STATUS verdict.
  2. GATE: a verdict cannot ship when its receipt disagrees with its expectation.
  3. OBSERVED DEFECT: the four instances above, all measured in this repo, none speculative.
  4. RETIREMENT: retire when every STATUS row's number is derived from a receipt produced by
     someone other than the row's author, making the agreement check redundant.

title: Resume-quality A/B: Jev-prune vs generic summary
description:
WHAT: Run the resume-quality A/B that decides whether Jev-pruning beats generic summarization on real omp traffic.
WHY: Step 1 proved size reduction (45%) with zero text loss, but reduction is not the claim — better-than-summary continuation is. Without this test a smaller context that answers worse would ship as a win.
APPROACH:
1. Corpus: compaction/fixtures/omp-session-big-20260917.jsonl via compaction/src/omp-adapter.ts. Arm A context = compactMessages() output (see compaction/runs/replay-big-20260917.json; re-derive, do not trust it).
2. Extract the 5 dropped call ids (dump decisions with a tsx one-liner against the real Jev client) and author 3 resume questions answerable ONLY from dropped results, with expected answers quoted from the fixture.
3. Arm B context: one generic condensation of the same transcript (fixed prompt, recorded in receipt; `omp -p`, default model).
4. Resume: one fresh model call per arm, identical prompt (context + questions). Record answers verbatim. Grade substring-match against expected.
BUDGET: ~4 live calls total (Arm A re-derive 1, summary 1, resume 2). State each call in the receipt.
NON-GOALS: No library changes. No new fixtures from other sessions. No prompt-tuning to make an arm win.
ACCEPTANCE: compaction/runs/ab-<date>.json with both contexts' byte sizes, both answer transcripts, per-question grades, and a one-line verdict (A wins / B wins / tie). Verdict must be reproducible from the receipt alone.
RECEIPT: The runs/ab JSON + close reason citing it. Report model names, Jev request count, and TYPESAFE_API_KEY sourcing (env only, never in tree).
close_reason: Receipt compaction/runs/ab-20260917.json; live verdict B wins (A 1/3, B 3/3), four live calls, commit e763fa3.

title: Lane gap: am mail leg of the REPLY-VIA contract is dead — 6 units delivered, inbox count 0
description:
WHAT
The three-leg callback contract (bead comment + am mail + committed receipt) has a silently dead
middle leg in this lane. Measured 2026-09-18 00:41Z: `am inbox --project ~/Developer/jev --agent
CyanFalcon` returned `"count": 0, "inbox": []` after panes 2 and 3 had delivered SIX units
between them. Every bead comment landed; every commit landed; not one mail arrived. Both panes
routed callbacks through the pane relay instead.

WHY
A three-leg contract with one dead leg is a two-leg contract that looks like three — the failure
mode the ntm-fleet-monitor skill names as 'a second leg catching the same fault hides a dead first
leg'. Worse here: mail is the only leg that reaches a conductor who is NOT reading this repo's git
log, so its death is invisible exactly when the lane is handed off. Today the conductor only learned
pane states by human chase.

Unknown which of three causes: (a) panes never ran leg 2; (b) the send ran but addressed a
non-existent recipient (agent-name mismatch — `am agents list` is the authority and CyanFalcon vs
the pane's own registered id may differ); (c) send succeeded and inbox read is scoped wrong.
Distinguishing these is the work.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Re-derive the denominator: `am inbox --project ~/Developer/jev --agent CyanFalcon` plus
   `am agents list ~/Developer/jev`, both quoted in the bead. State how many units had fired by then.
2. Positive control: send one mail from pane 1 to pane 1 and read it back. If that works, the send
   path is fine and the defect is (a) or (b). A zero without this control proves nothing.
3. Name the cause with evidence, not a guess.
4. If (b): the packet template in docs/demos/tick.md must carry the EXACT registered agent id, not a
   friendly name, and the fix is verified by one pane firing leg 2 successfully.
5. If (a): tick.md must require panes to report what the send returned (already added this session —
   verify the next callback carries it).
6. Re-run after fix: a subsequent unit's callback appears in `am inbox` with the bead id in the
   subject. Paste the row.
close_reason: docs/demos/duel-2/runs/mail-leg-ruling-20260918T154229Z.json fe045cd: both acceptance items met (denominator quoted, loopback control passed); ruled RETIRE with retry condition

comments.author: CyanFalcon
comments.text: PARTIAL — acceptance clauses 1-3 resolved by positive control. MEASURED this turn: am mail send from CyanFalcon TO CyanFalcon landed and am inbox --agent CyanFalcon went 0 -> 1. THE TRANSPORT WORKS. So cause (c) 'inbox read scoped wrong' is ELIMINATED, and cause (b) 'recipient name mismatch' is eliminated for at least ChartreuseTern, whose sends return a recipients list containing the name. Remaining cause is (a): the panes are not running leg 2. Also note the original measurement was partly MY instrument error — my own inbox reading 0 is EXPECTED, because I send to the conductor, not to myself; an empty inbox for the sender proves nothing about the sender's own sends. The real defect is narrower than filed: six units delivered and the conductor received bead comments and commits but no pane-originated mail. tick.md now requires panes to report what the send returned, and the pane-2 packet at this turn states the positive-control result so a missing mail is unambiguously a missed step. Re-verify on the next pane callback: if a pane's mail appears in its recipient's inbox, close; if not, the defect is in the pane's command form and the bead gets the exact failing invocation. NO-CLAIM: I did not observe a PANE-originated mail succeed or fail; I only proved the tool works for me.

title: A/B harness emits a one-word verdict over a nondeterministic arm — remove it or report a distribution
description:
WHAT
compaction/ab/run-ab.ts computes armB by a live runOmp summarization call with no temperature pin,
then at line 164 collapses the comparison to a single string: armAScore > armBScore ? 'A wins' :
armBScore > armAScore ? 'B wins' : 'tie'. Measured 2026-09-18 across three runs:

  ab-20260917         fixture 214,993 B sha 20fa1ea0   armA 1/3  armB 3/3  'B wins'
  ab-rerun-20260918   fixture  82,214 B sha 2346451d   armA 1/3  armB 1/3  'tie'
  ab-sample3-20260918 fixture  82,214 B sha 2346451d   armA 1/3  armB 3/3  'B wins'

Rows 2 and 3 are byte-identical in input and differ by two points on armB. armA scored 1/3 in all
three. So the verdict field flips on generator variance while reading like a result.

WHY
The 'B wins' string propagated into 17 tracked files — duel idea files, four score files, four
dispatch packets, a claim audit, and bead bodies — before anything ran the harness twice. A
one-word verdict over a stochastic arm is not a presentation problem; it manufactures a finding.
This is the lane's own 'cherry-picked N' violation committed by its own tooling, and the tooling is
what made it easy.

ACCEPTANCE
1. The harness no longer emits an unconditional 'verdict' string. Either (a) drop the field, or
   (b) emit it only when the run carries n>=10 samples per stochastic arm plus the observed spread,
   and refuse (nonzero) when asked for a verdict at n=1.
2. armA may still be reported absolutely — it is deterministic-enough (1/3, three for three) and
   that is the lane's one supported compaction finding.
3. The receipt records, per arm, whether the arm is deterministic, and for stochastic arms the
   sample count and the per-sample scores. A receipt that cannot express variance is the root cause.
4. RED arm: a fixture run twice with a stochastic arm and differing scores must NOT produce a
   verdict; the harness reports the spread and exits nonzero if a caller demanded one.
5. Re-run the existing three receipts' inputs under the new harness and confirm no 'B wins' or
   'tie' string is produced for n=1.
6. Every one of the 17 citing files is either corrected or annotated. Re-derive the count with
   'git ls-files -z | xargs -0 grep -lE "3/3|B wins|ab-20260917"' and quote the new number;
   EVAL.md, NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE.md R11 and WIZARD_IDEAS_CC.md are already done at 3234bce.
close_reason: DONE commit=ff99df8 receipt=compaction/runs/ab-verdict-migration-20260918.json. run-ab.ts now records per-arm sampling summaries and emits no relative verdict at n=1; --verdict exits 2 with spread evidence unless both arms have >=10 zero-spread samples. Existing three receipts mark historical verdicts retracted. Added red-arm and zero-spread tests: compaction npm test 20/20, npm run typecheck PASS, entrypoint tsc PASS, foundation/gates.sh ALL GREEN. Citation census re-derived at 34 lexical matches; authoritative EVAL/NEGATIVE_EVIDENCE/compaction docs corrected and historical Markdown/JSON citations annotated.

title: fleet-idle-monitor: reports the USER SHELL as actionable, and cannot express a dry queue (R10 retry fired, twice, independently)
description:
WHAT
Two independent findings this turn converge on the same upstream target: the shared installed
binary $HOME/.local/bin/fleet-idle-monitor, wired for jev at 549c40a on the identical row shape
both other lanes use, cannot express two things this lane needs.

FINDING 1 (conductor, measured 01:18Z) — it reports the USER SHELL as actionable work:
  IDLE_PROVEN session=jev pane=%70 age=2041s timer=prompt
  ACTIONABLE  session=jev pane=%70 bead=uds-ry5d mode=report-only
Pane identity, re-derived with `tmux list-panes -a -F '#{pane_id} idx=#{pane_index}
sess=#{session_name} cmd=#{pane_current_command}'`:
  %70 idx=0 sess=jev cmd=zsh   <- the user shell
  %74 idx=1 cli.js · %71 idx=2 cli.js · %73 idx=3 cli.js
So the single pane it recommends for work is Joshua's interactive shell, which is idle by
definition and which tick.md section 1 states must NEVER be dispatched. It also recommends
'uds-ry5d', a bead from a DIFFERENT project, for a jev pane — so bead selection is not
session-scoped either.

FINDING 2 (pane 2, dry-queue selection 735a158, receipt
docs/demos/duel-1/runs/queue-dry-20260918T012132Z.json) — it cannot express a DRY QUEUE. It
reports a pane as idle, but the lane needs to distinguish a pane idle because it finished from a
pane idle because its packet ran out of units. The second is a defect in the CONDUCTOR's packet,
not a pane state, and the two demand opposite responses: classify a receipt versus resend a queue.
Pane 2 rejected R7, R8, R9 and R11 as not-yet-satisfiable and selected R10 on this basis.

WHY
Today the wired mode is --report-only, so nothing is typed anywhere and no damage occurs; the
defect is a wrong recommendation. But the binary has a nudge mode, and anyone following the
ACTIONABLE line literally would dispatch into the user's shell. 'A bare shell is nobody to keep
alive' is already fleet doctrine; this is that rule failing in the installed artifact.

Both findings hit R10's recorded retry condition verbatim: 'the installed binary cannot express
something jev specifically needs'. Per R10 the remedy is a flag or an upstream bead against the
shared binary, NEVER a jev-local fork — the fork was already written, measured as worse (it read
safe_to_dispatch from a SINGLE capture, while the installed binary requires two), and withdrawn.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Re-derive the pane mapping with the tmux command above and quote it, naming which pane_index is
   the user shell.
2. Establish whether the binary already has an exclusion (a --workers flag, a pane_index filter, or
   an agent_type/pane_current_command check) and state which. cli.js panes carry an agent and zsh
   panes do not, so pane_current_command is a sufficient discriminator if nothing better exists.
3. If an exclusion exists: wire it into the jev cron row and prove %70 drops out of the report.
4. If it does not: file upstream against the binary's owning repo with this evidence, and until it
   lands treat the jev row's output as workers-only by convention, recorded in GATES.md.
5. For the dry-queue gap, decide and record WHERE it belongs: the binary cannot know a packet's
   unit count, so this is probably conductor-side state (a queue file with remaining units) rather
   than a monitor feature. Rejecting it as out-of-scope for the binary is a valid, preferred
   outcome — say so explicitly rather than leaving it open.
6. Determine whether bead=uds-ry5d is cross-project leakage or an intended global queue; if
   leakage, that is its own upstream finding.
7. RED arm: with the fix in place, a session whose only idle pane is the user shell must report OK /
   no actionable pane, never an ACTIONABLE row.

comments.author: CyanFalcon
comments.text: THIRD DEFECT in the same binary, found by Joshua observing what the instrument denied. It reported 'WORKING session=jev pane=%73 reason=timer_changed' while pane 3 was IDLE. Joshua: 'pane 3 has been kept idle'. %73 is idx=3 = pane 3 (tmux list-panes -a). The monitor's liveness signal was a changing content hash coming off an animating spinner — the documented trap that 'content-changed is necessary but not sufficient; a detector whose input animates on its own can never report idle'. This is the FAIL-OPEN direction and the expensive one: a false-IDLE costs one wasted nudge, a false-WORKING costs a whole pane sitting still while the conductor believes it is busy. It cost pane 3 roughly 35 minutes, and I compounded it by trusting the instrument over the artifact — the same error shape as reporting pane 3 'no callback yet' while its three commits sat in git log. So the bead now carries three defects against one binary: (1) reports the USER SHELL %70 idx=0 cmd=zsh as ACTIONABLE with a cross-project bead uds-ry5d; (2) cannot express a dry queue (pane 2, 735a158); (3) reports false-WORKING off spinner animation. Add to acceptance: a RED arm where a pane whose ONLY changing content is the spinner/status line must NOT report WORKING — the discriminators named in fleet doctrine are an advancing elapsed timer, an existing tool child via pgrep -P on the pane pid, or a visible state change on Esc. Routed to pane 2 for the read-only investigation of what exclusion/liveness mechanisms the binary already exposes, and to find the owning repo so the upstream bead has a destination. NO-CLAIM: I have not read the binary's source or probed its liveness logic; all three defects are observed BEHAVIOUR, and defect 3 is attributed to the spinner by mechanism-matching against doctrine, not by reading the code.

title: demo-1 BLOCKER: three artifacts assert three different turn counts for one fixture (6 vs 18 vs 1)
description:
WHAT
demos/routing-backtest disagrees with its own fixture about how many turns that fixture contains,
by 6x and 18x, and a stranger following the documented path cannot tell.

MEASURED 2026-09-18 from a CLEAN CLONE (git clone of the repo into a temp dir, install.sh run, then
the documented command):

  fixtures/real-excerpt-t1-t6.jsonl .......... 94 rows
  rows carrying a "model" field .............. 18   (all muse-spark-1.3-contributor)
  fixtures/manifest.json purpose ............. "happy-path corpus turns 1-6"
  reader output on that fixture .............. {"sessions":1,"turns":1,"classifiableTurns":1,"skippedTurns":0}

So the same file is described as 6 turns by the manifest, contains 18 model-bearing rows, and is
read as 1 turn by the demo. At most one of those can be right.

The same reader reports 30 turns over 2 real omp session logs, which is plausible, so the defect is
specific to how the fixture excerpt is segmented rather than a general failure. Most likely cause:
the excerpt contains one user prompt followed by many assistant/tool rows, so a turn-grouping rule
keyed on user prompts sees 1 turn while the manifest author counted assistant exchanges. That is a
HYPOTHESIS, not a finding — the code has not been read.

WHY THIS BLOCKS THE SHIP CLAIM
docs/demos/PLAN.md defines shipped as four artifacts and all four now exist: install.sh runs clean
on a fresh clone (10 pass / 0 fail, exit 0), a receipt exists, an EVAL row is appended, and tests
with RED arms fire. But the demo's ONE stranger-reachable result is n=1, and its own manifest says
it should be 6. A stranger runs the documented command, gets turns:1, and has no way to know
whether that is the corpus, the reader, or a bug. "An empty scan set is an ERROR, not a pass" has a
sibling this lane had not written down: A ONE-TURN SCAN SET IS NOT A DEMONSTRATION.

It also means the demo's headline finding — actual $7.230350988 vs counterfactual $7.226928188,
savings $0.0034228, 0.047% over 30 turns — is reproducible only against ~/.omp session logs that no
stranger has. The shipped fixtures cannot reproduce the result the demo is about.

ACCEPTANCE
1. Re-derive all three counts and quote them: fixture rows, model-bearing rows, manifest claim,
   reader output. State which is authoritative and why.
2. Fix the disagreement at its source. Either the manifest's "turns 1-6" is wrong and becomes the
   measured number, or the reader's turn segmentation is wrong and is corrected. Do not "fix" it by
   editing whichever artifact is easier.
3. Define "turn" once, in one place, and make both the reader and the fixture READMEs cite that
   definition. Three artifacts asserting three counts is a missing shared definition, not three
   bugs.
4. The stranger path must produce a NON-VACUOUS result: a fixture that yields enough turns to show
   a cheap-vs-frontier split, with at least one routable turn. Re-run from a clean clone and paste
   the denominator.
5. RED arm: a run whose classifiable-turn count is below a stated floor must WARN or ERROR rather
   than emit a receipt that looks like a successful backtest. n=1 must not read as a pass.
6. install.sh's closing message currently ends with a placeholder,
   "npm run backtest -- <session.jsonl>...". Replace it with the exact copy-pasteable command
   against a shipped fixture, per the no-placeholders rule. A stranger should not have to guess an
   argument.

title: Foundry bug: house-gate selftests fail under init.templateDir (needs git-config isolation)
description:
WHAT: report and fix upstream that loop-kit gate selftests which build a throwaway git fixture repo fail on any machine with `init.templateDir` set.

WHY: measured 2026-09-17 on this machine. `init.templateDir = ~/.git-templates` installs the commit-msg verification-level hook into EVERY newly created repo, so a selftest that inits a temp repo and commits plain fixture messages dies at "SELFTEST FAIL: fixture repo setup" - the hook correctly refuses a level-less subject.   GIT_CONFIG_GLOBAL=/dev/null GIT_CONFIG_SYSTEM=/dev/null ... --selftest -> PASS (3 known-bad flagged, 3 clean controls passed)
So the FIXTURE was broken, not the gate - and every future gate with the same shape inherits the defect. Our wrapper (foundation/gates.d/50-house-gates.sh) already neutralizes the config; the fix belongs upstream so the whole fleet gets it.

ACCEPTANCE: loop-kit gate selftests pass with ambient config on a machine with init.templateDir set - by isolating git config or committing with --no-verify inside the fixture. Verify by running `commit-evidence-lint.sh --selftest` with NO env overrides and getting SELFTEST PASS.

title: timeout-leak.test.mjs latency floor (40 ms) sits above guardedFetch's own deadline (timeoutMs-25 = 25 ms): flaky
description:
WHAT: work/jev-client/test/timeout-leak.test.mjs:35 asserts latencyMs >= 40 with timeoutMs 50, but work/jev-client/src/index.ts guardedFetch aborts at Math.max(1, timeoutMs - 25) = 25 ms (introduced 679e5f4). The test passes only when overhead adds >= 15 ms. Measured 2026-09-24 on one M3 Ultra under sibling load: pre-lazy-import client (1c6d23d~1) 7/12 and 7/12 pass; current client 6/12 (script /tmp/rsr-timeout-ab.sh, recorded in the jev-lcf receipt).

comments.text: MaintFixes, fixed in 454cfb3 (pushed). ROOT CAUSE (probed with /tmp/maintfixes-rw2-probe2.mjs, 3x12 requests on Node): the headers-then-hang server usually ends on the SDK's OWN 50 ms timer in bufferResponse at about 51-58 ms, because guardedFetch returns once headers arrive and clears its timer. The guard's 25 ms deadline wins only when headers are slow, error 'Connection error: Request timed out after 50ms.' at about 34 ms, and that is exactly when the fixed 40 ms floor failed. So the old test flaked only on the path the fix exists for. FIX: index.ts exports guardDeadlineMs(timeoutMs), now used by guardedFetch's setTimeout. The test asserts error matches /timed out/ AND latencyMs >= guardDeadlineMs(50)-5, with 5 ms tolerance for Date.now truncation and libuv's cached-loop-time timer start. It also adds a no-headers hang server that forces the guard path on all 8 requests; the original headers-then-hang case stays. PRE-FIX (/tmp/maintfixes-rw2-loop.sh, M3 Ultra under sibling load, 2026-09-24): node 18/30 pass (12 fails at latencyMs 28-38), bun 23/30 (7 fails at 29-38). POST-FIX, same script, 50 consecutive runs each: node 50/50 pass, bun 50/50 pass. PLANT: a throw at the top of guardedFetch's body, before fetch, in scratch copy /tmp/maintfixes-rw2-plant (HEAD + my hunks) gives node rc=1 fail 2/2 and bun rc=1 fail 2/2 ('error=Connection error: planted: returned before fetch'). Unplanted scratch: rc=0 pass 2/2. All jev-client tests: node --test work/jev-client/test/*.test.mjs gives 51/51 in the worktree, which includes BillingUnits' uncommitted index.ts edits. NO-CLAIM: no 50x loop was run against the committed blob by itself; the 50x loops ran in the shared worktree. (3) What the test measures: it does NOT observe the timer being cleared. Its no-vacuous-pass check is error /timed out/ + latency >= guardDeadlineMs(50)-5 = 20 ms, the floor now derived from the client (so a change inside guardDeadlineMs moves the floor with it; a literal change is caught).
